comment: Per-page ceilings on local CSS+JS: the number of requests and their total uncompressed bytes. Seeded from the measured weight on 2026-08-29 with ~15% headroom, so a page cannot quietly double. This is a ratchet, not a target - lowering a ceiling after real work is welcome; raising one means saying why in the commit. The site has no build step, so these are the bytes a visitor actually fetches.
note: modules/roadmap/index.html is the outlier on every axis and the only page over 250KB. The two console-snippet tools were merged into one file on 2026-08-30, which took a request and ~2.6KB off every protected page; these ceilings were re-seeded from that.
note-platform: modules/platform/index.html was raised from 202000/24 to 212000/26 on 2026-09-07. The page went from one flat column to three navigable views with a sidebar index, a filter toolbar and collapsed cards, and its single module split into four (shell, views, cards, knowledge) because one file carrying all of it would have passed the 600-line hard cap in tests/size-budget.json. The bytes bought the fix for the page's actual problem - 46 capabilities rendered fully open in one scroll - so the trade is deliberate. Two of the requests are the new modules; the sidebar shell moved to components.css rather than adding a fifth.
note-roadmap: modules/roadmap/index.html was raised to 385000/42 on 2026-09-15 for the Sprint Roadmap, then LOWERED back to the original 369000/40 on 2026-09-16 when the sprint views moved to their own page (modules/sprints/). The page gave back the two requests it had taken and now measures 37 requests and 343,968 bytes. A ratchet is meant to come down after real work, and this is what that looks like: the ceiling follows the page rather than the page growing into the ceiling. It remains the outlier on every axis.
note-sprints: modules/sprints/index.html was raised from 26/252,000 to 30/305,000 on 2026-09-16 when the roadmap's detail drawer was added to it. The owner asked that a bar open detail in place rather than sending the reader to another page, and the drawer is five files: roadmap-detail.css, detail.js, drawer.js, lazy-detail.js and work-items-data.js. Nothing was duplicated to do it - it is the same drawer over the same rows, which is the whole reason it costs what it costs. Measures 28 requests and 279,383 bytes. The page still reads far less DATA than the roadmap: it fetches the two dozen rows this board draws, not the whole work set. Raised again to 31/330,000 on 2026-09-17 for the presentation overhaul that made the board readable from a projector. Two files, both splits this repo had already written down rather than new surface: assets/css/sprint-cards.css and assets/js/pages/roadmap/views-sprint-cards.js are the card half of a board sheet and a board module that tests/size-budget.json named as seams before the work started. Nothing was duplicated to take them - the cards moved out whole, and the board kept the coordinate model it already shared with the roadmap. Measures 31 requests and 319,748 bytes. Raised again to 338,000 on 21 Sep 2026, requests UNCHANGED at 31: the sprint board gained three readings it could not carry before - what shape a stream is (does it end), the ceilings it lifts, and the column axis read as a priority scale rather than as sprints. All three went into files the page already loads, which is why the request count did not move: the rules are in sprints.css and sprint-cards.css, the builders in views-sprint.js and views-sprint-cards.js. Measures 331,434 bytes. The headroom is deliberately small - this page is second only to the roadmap and the next addition should have to justify itself. Raised to 32/352,000 on 23 Sep 2026 for one file, assets/js/pages/roadmap/detail-brief.js: the drawer's "Where it stands" section, which states the current plan for a row (sprint, step in its stream, who builds it, what is still open) so the owner no longer has to read the historic record to find it. It is its own file because detail.js sits past its 550-line revisit trigger, and the roadmap page loads it too, so both drawers answer the question the same way. Measures 32 requests and 350,045 bytes.
